source_text: Adhuc adiciam illam quoque partem in qua dum haereticus quasi oculo quodam gaudet proprio, ueritatis et luminis amisso, totam caecitatem sui agnoscat erroris. identidem enim et frequenter opponit quia dictum sit: sano tempore uobiscum sum, et non agnoscitis me? Philippe, qui uidit me, uidit et patrem. sed quod non intellegit, discat. culpatur Philippus, et iure quidem meritoque, quia dixerit: domine, ostende nobis patrem, et sufficit nobis. quando enim ex Christo aut audierat istud aut didicerat, quasi esset pater Christus, cum contra magis, quod filius esset, non quia pater, frequenter audisset, et saepe didicisset? quod enim dixit dominus, s me cognouistis, et patrem meum cognouistis, et a modo nostis illum, et uidistis illum, non sic dixerat ut se patrem uellet intellegi, sed quoniam qui penitus et plene et cum tota fide et tota religione accessit ad dei filium, omnibus modis per ipsum filium, in quem sic credit, ad patrem peruenturus sit, eundemque uisurus. nemo enim, inquit, potest uenire ad patrem nisi per me, et ideo ad patrem deum non tantum uenturus est, et cogniturus ipsum patrem, sed etiam sic tenere debet, atque ita animo ac mente praesumere, quasi iam nouerit patrem pariter et uiderit. Saepe enim scriptura diuina, quae nondum facta pro factis annuntiat, quia sic futura sunt, et quae omnibus modis fieri habent, non quasi futura sint, praedicat, sed quasi facta sint, narrat. denique cum nondum temporibus Isaiae prophetae Christus natus fuisset, quia puer, aiebat, natus est nobis; et cum nondum accessum esset ad Mariam, e accessit ad propheten, dicebat, e concepit, et peperit filium. et cum nondum sinum patris Christus exposuisset, referebat: e uocabitur nomen eius magni consili angelus. et cum nondum fuisset passus, guas? outs, pronuntiabat, ad iugulationem adductus est. et cum adhuc crux nusquam esset, aiebat: Tota die expandi manus meas ad populum non credentem., et cum nondum iniuriose potatus fuisset, s7fz, ait, mea potauerunt me aceto. et cum spoliatus adhuc non fuisset, dicebat, super uestem meam miserunt sortem: et dinumerauerunt ossa mea: effoderunt manus meas et pedes. prouidens enim scriptura diuina pro factis dicit, quae futura scit, et pro perfectis dicit, quae futura habet, quae sine dubitatione uentura sunt. et ideo dominus in praesenti loco dicebat: a modo nostis illum, et uidistis. dicebat enim uisum iri ab eo patrem, quisquis filium secutus fuisset; non quasi filius ipse esset pater uisus, sed quod praemium consecuturus esset, quisquis illum sequi et discipulus eius esse uoluisset, ut uidere patrem posset. nam et imago est dei patris, ut his etiam illud accedat, quoniam sicut pater operatur, ita operatur et filius, et imitator est filius omnium operum paternorum; ut perinde habeat unusquisque, quasi iam uiderit patrem, dum eum uidet qui inuisibilem patrem in omnibus operibus semper imitatur. Ceterum si ipse pater est Christus, quomodo confestim adicit et dicit: gud credit in me, opera quae ego facio et ipse Faciet, et maiora his faciet, quia ego ad patrem uado? et adhuc subnectit: si diligitis me, praecepta mea seruate: et ego rogabo patrem, et alium aduocatum dabit uobis. post quae etiam illud subnectit: s quis me diligit, sermonem meum custodiet: et pater meus diliget illum, et ad eum ueniemus, et mansionem apud illum Jaciemus. nec non etiam subdidit illud quoque: aduocatus autem ille spiritus sanctus, quem missurus est pater, ille uos docebit et commemorabit- omnia quaecumque dixero. praemittit adhuc istum locum, quo ostendat se esse filium, et merito subdidit, et dicit: s me diligeretis, gauderetis, quia eo ad patrem: quia pater maior me est. quid autem cum etiam ila subnectit: ego sum uitis uera, et pater meus agricola: omne sarmentum in me non afferens fructum tollit illud, et omne fructtSerum purgat, ut fructum ampliorem ferat? instat adhuc et adicit: sicut dilexit me pater, et ego dilexi uos; manete in mea caritate; si mandata mea seruaueritis, manebitis in mea caritale, sicut ego patris mandata seruaui, et maneo in eius caritate. adhuc ingerit, et dicit: dixi autem uos amicos, quia omnia quae audiui a patre meo, nota uobis feci. aggregat etiam hoc: sed haec omnia facient uobis propter nomen meum, quia ignorant eum qui me misit. Haec ergo numquam post illa euidenter illum non patrem sed filium esse testantia dominus subdidisset, si aut patrem se esse meminisset, aut patrem se uellet intellegi. nisi quoniam ut illud exprimeret, perinde unumquemque iam habere debere, dum imaginem dei patris per filium uidet, atque si uiderit patrem—quandoquidem unusquisque credens in filium exerceatur in imaginis contemplatione, ut assuefactus ad diuinitatem uidendam imagine proficere possit et crescere usque ad dei patris omnipotentis perfectam contemplationem,—et quoniam, qui hoc animo ac mentecombiberit et de omnibus sic futurum esse crediderit, patrem, quem uisurus sit, quasi iam quodammodo uiderit et hic iam sic habeat, quasi teneat, quod habiturum se pro certo sciat. Ceterum, si ipse pater fuisset, quid quasi futurum praemium repromittebat, quod iam praestiterat et dederat? nam quoniam dicit: beati mundo corde, quia ipsi deum uidebunt, polliceri deprehenditur contemplationem et aspectum patris. ergo nondum dederat: cur enim repromitteret, si iam dedisset? dederat enim, si pater esset; uidebatur enim, et contingebatur. quando autem, dum contingitur ipse Christus et uidetur, repromittit tamen et dicit, quoniam qui mundo fuerit corde, deum uidebit, hoc ipso probat patrem se non esse, qui tunc praesens cum uideretur repromittebat, quod patrem uisurus esset quisquis mundo corde fuisset. erat ergo repromittens haec non pater sed filius; quia qui filius erat, quod uideri habebat repromittebat: cuius repromissio superuacua fuisset, nisi filius fuisset. cur enim repromittebat mundis ut uiderent patrem, Si iam tunc qui praesentes erant, patrem Christum uidebant? sed quia filius erat, non pater, merito et filius, quia imago dei, tunc uidebatur, et pater, quia inuisibilis, mundis corde, ut uideretur, repromittitur et notatur. Haec igitur satis sit etiam aduersus istum haereticum dictasse, pauca de multis. campus enim, et quidem latus ac fusus, aperietur, plenius haereticum istum si agitare uoluerimus; quandoquidem duobus istis locis quibusdam effossis luminibus orbatus, totus sit in doctrinae suae caecitate superatus.
pass_a_gloss: I will add that part also in which, while the heretic, as it were, rejoices with his own eye, having lost the truth and light, may recognize the total blindness of his error. For he frequently and repeatedly objects that it was said: I am with you in healthy times, and you do not recognize me? Philip, who saw me, saw the Father also. But what he does not understand, let him learn. Philip is blamed, and rightly and deservedly, because he said: Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us. For when did he hear or learn from Christ that Christ was the Father, since, on the contrary, he heard and learned more frequently that He was the Son, not the Father? For what the Lord said, If you have known me, you have known my Father also, and from now on you know Him, and you have seen Him, He did not say in such a way that He wanted to be understood as the Father, but because whoever approaches the Son of God with total faith and total devotion will come to the Father through the Son, in whom he believes, and will see Him. For no one, He says, can come to the Father except through me, and therefore he who comes to God the Father will not only come and know the Father, but also ought to hold and presume in his mind and heart as if he already knew the Father and saw Him. For divine Scripture often announces what has not yet been done as if it were already done, because it will be so, and what will happen in all ways, it predicts not as if it were going to happen, but narrates as if it had already happened. Finally, when Christ had not yet been born in the time of the prophet Isaiah, it said: A child has been born to us, and before He had approached Mary, it said to the prophet: He has approached and conceived and borne a son. And when Christ had not yet exposed His breast, it said: His name will be called the Angel of great counsel. And when He had not yet suffered, it said: He was led to slaughter. And when the cross did not yet exist, it said: I have stretched out my hands all day to a disobedient people. And when He had not yet been given vinegar to drink, it said: They gave me vinegar to drink. And when He had not yet been stripped, it said: They cast lots for my garment and counted my bones and pierced my hands and feet. For divine Scripture speaks of what will be done as if it were already done, and of what will be perfect as if it were already perfect, what will come without doubt. And therefore the Lord said in this place: From now on you know Him and have seen Him, for He said that the Father would be seen by whoever followed the Son, not that the Son Himself was the Father seen, but that whoever followed Him and wanted to be His disciple would receive the reward of seeing the Father. For the Son is the image of God the Father, so that it may be added that just as the Father works, so also the Son works, and the Son is the imitator of all the Father's works, so that each one may have it as if he had already seen the Father, while seeing Him who always imitates the invisible Father in all His works. But if Christ Himself were the Father, how could He immediately add and say: He who believes in me will do the works that I do, and greater works than these, because I am going to the Father? And He also adds: If you love me, keep my commandments, and I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate. And after these things, He also adds: If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him. And He also adds: The Advocate is the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send, and He will teach you and remind you of all that I have said. He anticipates this place to show that He is the Son, and rightly adds and says: If you loved me, you would rejoice, because I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I. And what about when He also adds: I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer, and every branch that does not bear fruit in me, He takes away, and every fruitful branch, He purifies, so that it may bear more fruit? He also adds: As the Father loved me, I have loved you, abide in my love, if you keep my commandments, you will abide in my love, as I have kept my Father's commandments and abide in His love. He also says: I have called you friends, because all that I heard from my Father, I have made known to you. He also adds: But they will do all these things to you on account of my name, because they do not know Him who sent me. Therefore, the Lord would not have added these things, which clearly testify that He is not the Father but the Son, if He had remembered that He was the Father or wanted to be understood as the Father. But rather, He wanted to express that each one ought to have it as if he had already seen the Father, while seeing the image of God the Father through the Son, and as if he had seen the Father, since each believer in the Son is exercised in the contemplation of the image, so that, having become accustomed to seeing the divinity in the image, he may progress and grow until he reaches the perfect contemplation of God the Father Almighty. But if He Himself were the Father, what reward would He promise as if it were going to happen, when He had already given and granted it? For since He says: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God, He is found to promise the contemplation and sight of the Father. Therefore, He had not yet given it, for why would He promise it if He had already given it? He would have given it if He were the Father, for He would have been seen and touched. But when Christ, while being touched and seen, still promises and says that whoever is pure in heart will see God, this very thing proves that He is not the Father, who, being present and seen, promises what He will see, namely, the Father. Therefore, it was not the Father but the Son who was promising these things, because, being the Son, He was promising what He had to be seen, and His promise would have been unnecessary if He were not the Son. For why would He promise the pure in heart that they would see the Father, if those who were present were already seeing the Father, Christ? But because He was the Son, not the Father, and rightly the Son, because He is the image of God, He was seen at that time, and the Father, because He is invisible, is promised to the pure in heart, that He may be seen. These things, then, are enough, even against this heretic, to have said a few things out of many. For the field, and indeed a broad and spacious one, will be opened if we want to discuss this heretic further, since, having been blinded by the removal of two passages, he has been completely overcome by the blindness of his doctrine.
